artifacts.title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Knox Baird and other elders challenged Grace Presbytery's handling of complaints, BCO 40-5 review requests, document demands, and a stay of pending trials arising from conflict at First Presbyterian Church of Hattiesburg. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, rejected one specification, and did not reach another; concurring opinions were recorded.

artifacts.title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaints of TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery (cases 2007-09 and 2007-10). KEP erred when it empowered the Pulpit Commission to act on behalf of the church session without proper consent, and erred when it filed a civil action against TE Lee to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The decision affirms the non-hierarchical, voluntary nature of the PCA and its limited jurisdiction in civil matters.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained two consolidated complaints by TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery, annulling KEP's actions in empowering a Pulpit (Stated Supply Approval) Commission to act on behalf of the HKPC session without congregational consent, and annulling KEP's filing of a civil lawsuit in New Jersey state court to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The opinion extensively discusses the non-hierarchical nature of PCA polity and the limits of a presbytery's authority over local congregations.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: Frank J. Smith challenged Northeast Presbytery's actions surrounding the dissolution of Grace Presbyterian Church and the administration of its former members. The SJC denied the complaint by a 20-2 vote, with a dissent disputing the majority's treatment of the complainant's constitutional and procedural claims.
